candidates.title: Inventory denial + merchant spam via soft stock-reservation abuse across self-registered customer accounts
candidates.description: Mechanism (fully source-grounded): (1) POST /api/customer-auth/register/ — CustomerRegisterThrottle scope 'register' = 10/hour keyed by IP, NO captcha on registration. (2) POST /api/stores/public/<slug>/orders/ requires only IsCustomer — no email_verified check anywhere in the order path (email_verified only gates lifecycle emails). (3) OrderCreateThrottle = 10/hour keyed by request.user.pk = customer.pk, NOT IP — one IP can mint ~10 accounts/hour -> ~100 orders/hour. (4) Captcha is deterministic arithmetic — scriptable speed bump, not a bot barrier. (5) Each order claims soft stock: claimed_quantities sums OrderItem.qty over ALL PENDING_PAYMENT orders with expires_at > now regardless of which customer owns them; _resolve_lines rejects any buyer whose qty > stock - claimed. (6) Per-order claim ceiling MAX_ITEMS=50 x MAX_QTY=100 = 5000 units per product-set; default reservation window 48h, owner-configurable to 720h; claims auto-release at expires_at so sustaining the DoS needs only continuous re-ordering at 10/h/account. (7) Every fake order fires owner 'created' notification + owner email -> 10 merchant emails/hour/account. Impact: a single scripted account can keep low-stock SKUs permanently 'sold out' to legitimate buyers and spam the merchant inbox; ~10 accounts/hour per IP scales linearly. Cost to attacker: zero (orders just expire unpaid). Blocked fact: deployed throttle enforcement (Redis fail-open is deliberate), real captcha practicality, and expire_orders cron cadence are not source-visible.
candidates.root_cause: Stock reservations are claimed per-order globally (claimed_quantities counts every customer's PENDING_PAYMENT orders) while order creation is gated only by per-customer-pk throttle + scriptable arithmetic captcha + uncaptcha'd registration — no per-IP order throttle, no email_verified requirement, and no per-store pending-order cap.
candidates.intended_behavior: Stock claims should require a minimally-verified principal (email_verified or equivalent) and/or orders should be throttled per-IP/per-store with a cap on simultaneous pending reservations per store, so anonymous-scale account minting cannot monopolize inventory.

hardening: Proof-upload race (orders/views/public.py:216-279): status/payment_method/hasattr(order,'proof') checked before the Store->Order lock and never re-validated under it. An order transitioning to CANCELLED/EXPIRED between fast-path check and lock gets a PaymentProof created after release_proof already ran -> orphaned row + R2 object + consumed quota. Window sub-second; bounded by 10/h/IP and 4MB. Re-check locked_order.status/payment_method inside the atomic.

Wrap claim access.

Throttle namespace collision: ResilientUserRateThrottle keys throttle_user_<pk>; request.user can be a Customer (pk space) or auth.User (same pk space) on different endpoints sharing the 'user' 1000/day scope (e.g., cart views have no throttle_classes -> defaults apply).
